tips.title: Pick the highest rung you can
tips.text: For most trips the order runs: walking and cycling first, then trains and buses, then a shared car, then a solo car, with flying last. Choose the highest rung your trip allows.

tips.title: Prefer trains for medium distances
tips.text: Where a railway exists, trains usually beat driving alone and flying on both comfort and impact — and the journey becomes part of the trip.

tips.title: Pack light
tips.text: Every extra kilo is carried by your transport the whole way; a lighter bag is a small saving multiplied by every kilometre.

tips.title: Fly less, stay longer
tips.text: One two-week stay instead of two weekend flights halves the flying for the same days away.

tips.title: Choose stays that prove it
tips.text: Look for accommodation with third-party certification — the Brand Directory module explains the labels — or locally owned guesthouses that keep money in the community.

tips.title: Leave places as you found them
tips.text: Carry a reusable bottle and bag while travelling, refuse single-use plastics, and stick to marked paths in natural areas.
